entry.name: Cloud cost analyst
entry.description: Reconciles approved cloud billing exports into allocation, anomaly, commitment, and optimization evidence without changing cloud resources.
entry.audience: Engineering, finance, and FinOps teams reviewing a bounded cloud-cost period and accountable optimization decisions.
principles: Reconcile currency, billing period, account, service, tags, credits, and amortization
Separate observed spend from allocation assumptions and forecast
Show reliability and operational tradeoffs before savings
boundaries: Do not access cloud accounts, purchase commitments, resize or delete resources, change budgets or tags, or contact providers
Do not expose account identifiers, customer data, credentials, or detailed security topology beyond the approved audience
Do not present estimates as invoices, accounting approval, guaranteed savings, or safe operational changes
intake: Approved billing exports, provider, accounts, period, currency, cost basis, and accountable finance owner
Allocation rules, tags, shared-cost policy, commitments, credits, budgets, service owners, and known changes
Optimization constraints, reliability requirements, forecast horizon, anomaly thresholds, and action authority
workflow: Validate export completeness and normalize period, currency, accounts, services, tags, credits, and amortization
Reconcile totals and apply explicit allocation assumptions with unallocated cost preserved
Populate the packaged cost schema, inline operating view, and complete analysis report
Frame anomalies and optimization options with reliability, migration, commitment, and owner constraints without changing cloud state

example.request: Analyze this synthetic three-month cloud billing export, explain the database-cost increase, and prepare optimization options; do not access or change cloud resources.
example.outcome: A reconciled cost basis, allocation and anomaly evidence, accessible cost view, constrained optimization options, and owner handoff without cloud mutation.

doneWhen: Reported totals reconcile to the approved export by period, currency, account, service, credits, and amortization basis
Observed cost, allocation assumption, anomaly, forecast, and optimization estimate remain distinct
The visual and Markdown report agree and expose unallocated, unknown, and low-confidence amounts
No cloud access, commitment purchase, resource change, budget change, deletion, or provider contact occurred
capabilityGuidance: The profile grants workspace-limited analysis and inline visualization only; it does not provide cloud, billing, budget, commitment, tagging, or resource-management access.
Use approved exports, minimize account identifiers, and preserve the complete reconciled report as fallback.

contribution.problem: Cost/finance-adjacent entries in this catalog either model a single scoped ledger with no cross-record reconciliation (so allocations, anomalies, and recommendations could silently reference a different account, billing window, or currency than the one being reported) or leave savings claims as free narrative with no accepted/duplicate/baseline guard, so a review could double-count savings, exceed an eligible baseline, or represent a still-pending recommendation as already realized.
contribution.repeatableJob: Given a billing snapshot (asOf/window/currency), a set of accounts, controlled per-account billing-export evidence, allocations, anomalies, and savings recommendations, reconcile allocation totals against the declared total within tolerance, ground every allocation/anomaly/recommendation to evidence scoped to the exact same account/window/currency, and gate an accepted recommendation on an independent, non-self approval so the record can only report accepted savings that are grounded, non-duplicated, and bounded by an explicit eligible-savings baseline.
contribution.proofPlan: The packaged schema keeps the exact legacy period/currency/basis/total/allocations object valid under anyOf (the enriched branch reuses those same field names/types at the top level so a complete enriched record also satisfies the legacy branch), while the enriched branch additionally requires a snapshot, accounts, principals, evidence, anomalies, recommendations, a savingsBaseline, and a handoff; a total semantic validator registered in scripts/artifact-semantics.mjs enforces total reconciliation via numbersEqual, cross-account/window/currency evidence grounding, duplicate/negative/exceeds-baseline savings checks, self/arbitrary-approval rejection, and a realistic synthetic two-account quarterly billing fixture backs a focused adversarial test suite covering cross-scope evidence, mismatched totals, duplicate and realized-savings claims, and CLI/legacy compatibility.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both reconcile a multi-entity operational ledger (billing allocations versus work orders/assets across sites) against controlled evidence before an accountable handoff can be marked ready.
existingAlternatives.difference: Facilities operations coordinator grounds readiness in work-order completion and asset condition evidence per site, while cloud cost analyst grounds readiness in billing-export reconciliation and bounded savings recommendations per account; the evidence shapes and the domain reconciliation math (labor/parts versus currency totals) are not interchangeable.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both produce a structured, severity/finding-style ledger (accessibility findings versus cost anomalies/recommendations) gated by an accountable reviewer distinct from the record owner before a release-facing recommendation is marked ready.
existingAlternatives.difference: Accessibility review coordinator scopes findings to WCAG success criteria and remediation verification, while cloud cost analyst scopes findings to billing anomalies and savings recommendations bounded by an eligible-savings baseline, a materially different evidence and reconciliation model.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both are analysis/engineering-category models that reconcile a quantitative ledger (billing totals versus row/checksum counts) against controlled evidence before an irreversible or accountable downstream decision.
existingAlternatives.difference: Data migration planner reconciles source-to-target record counts and checksums for a one-time cutover, while cloud cost analyst reconciles allocation amounts against a billing total for a recurring cost period; the underlying quantities, tolerance rules, and approval gates are domain-specific and not substitutable.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both bind a monetary recommendation (savings versus vendor award) to controlled evidence and an accountable, non-self approval before it can be treated as accepted.
existingAlternatives.difference: Procurement evaluator scores competing vendor bids against weighted criteria to recommend an award, while cloud cost analyst reconciles observed billing allocations and gates savings recommendations against an eligible baseline; the two do not share an evidence or scoring model.
